title: Check a thread's life story

blocks.text: The page's transition table, and its answer to "can a thread go directly from `BLOCKED` to `WAITING`?": **no**, a thread must be `RUNNABLE` to call `wait()`, `join()` or `park()`. But `WAITING` to `BLOCKED` **is** possible: a thread notified in `Object.wait()` must re-enter the monitor, and while another thread holds it, it is `BLOCKED`.

Write `Lifecycle.isValid(List<Thread.State> states)`: the states one thread entered, in order. It is valid when it is not empty, starts at `NEW`, and each state follows the one before it by a transition in the table. A thread need not have ended yet, so the list may stop anywhere.

cases.says: A sequence of states made only of the page's transitions, starting at NEW, is valid; one with a transition the table lacks is not.
BLOCKED goes only to RUNNABLE: a thread must run again before it can wait.
WAITING or TIMED_WAITING may go straight to BLOCKED, when a notified thread must re-enter a held monitor.
A life starts at NEW, never returns to it, and nothing follows TERMINATED.

concepts: NEW is left once by start(), and TERMINATED is permanent.
A thread must be RUNNABLE to start waiting, so BLOCKED never goes straight to WAITING, while a notified waiter may go straight to BLOCKED.
